title: Prompt Orchestration Rulebook — personal notebook
content:
Purpose: riffing on a compact, operational 'rulebook' for client-side + service orchestration of prompts. Mostly a personal notebook: experiments, config sketches, quick ASCII diagrams, and open questions. Not for prod yet.

Quick summary / motivation:
- We need a small, composable policy layer that sits between callers (SDKs, clients) and model endpoints to manage: cost vs latency tradeoffs, context trimming, fallback semantics, and multi-model orchestration (stitching, reranking).
- Goal: let product teams encode high-level goals (e.g., `maximize-latency-slo: 300ms` or `preserve-critical-context: true`) and have the runtime enforce them via a compact rule set.

Design constraints / non-goals:
- Must be lightweight (applies per-call with minimal overhead).
- Prefer declarative config that can be shipped as part of route definitions or inline at call-time.
- Non-goal: full policy engine with hierarchical inheritance on day 1. Keep it local-first.

High-level API shape (sketch) — single endpoint that accepts a prompt + rulebook reference:
POST /v1/orchestrate
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <key>
Body: {
  "prompt": "string or array of blocks",
  "context": {"recent_messages": [...], "user_profile": {...}},
  "rulebook": "inline|id|url",
  "client_hints": {"preferred_latency_ms": 250, "cost_budget_cents": 5}
}

Response: {
  "id": "orchestration-<uuid>",
  "stages": [ {"stage": "cache-check", "result": "miss"}, ... ],
  "final_response": {"text": "...", "model": "llama-3-13b-q"},
  "reasoning_trace": ["trimmed-context: 2200->1024 tokens", "reranked: model-b recommended on quality/cost"]
}

Rulebook DSL (small YAML-ish sketch):
- name: web-search-augmented-short
  goals:
    - conserve_tokens: true
    - latency_slo_ms: 300
  stages:
    - name: prefetch-knowledge
      action: call-external (search)
      timeout_ms: 80
      fallback: skip
    - name: context-normalize
      action: trim-by-priority
      params:
        keep: ["system_prompt", "last_user_message", "entities"]
        max_tokens: 800
    - name: model-dispatch
      strategies:
        - prefer: low_cost_variant
          when: client_hints.cost_budget_cents < 10
        - prefer: fast_variant
          when: client_hints.preferred_latency_ms < 150
    - name: rerank
      action: rerank-responses
      params: {metric: "semantic-similarity", threshold: 0.78}

Notes on DSL semantics (rough):
- Stages run top->down; each stage can short-circuit on `fatal` or `satisfy_goal`
- `fallback` for a stage can be `skip`, `degrade` (weaker behavior), or `escalate` (invoke different flow)
- Actions are pluggable: `call-external`, `trim-by-priority`, `synthesize-prompt`, `parallel-model-fanout`, `stitch-fragments`, `rerank-responses`

Cost-aware routing heuristic (experiment idea):
- Track per-route `expected_token_cost_ms` and `p99_latency_ms` for model variants.
- When cost_budget is tight, prefer models with lower tokens-per-generation and apply stronger prefix caching.
- If latency SLO tight, pick lower-context variants and optionally do synchronous partial results (stream first chunk from small model, refine with larger model asynchronously).

ASCII architecture sketch:
client-sdk -> orchestrator-rulebook -> request-middleware -> routing-layer -> {cache, prefetch, model-cluster}
                                        |
                                        +-> telemetry: trace-id, reason-steps, cost-estimate

Example: short-circuiting flow for mobile client (scenario)
- mobile client with preferred_latency_ms=150 and cost_budget_cents=3
- Rulebook picks: skip prefetch, aggressive trimming (keep last message + system), prefer quantized 8-bit model on local dedicated pool.
- If model latency > 200ms for p95, fallback to server-side distilled model with snapshot stitching.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How much logic should the client SDK hold vs server rulebook? Tradeoffs: offline mode requires client rules, but model updates / rollouts want central authority. Hybrid?
- Canonical representation for "priority list" when trimming context: should priorities be named tokens (system/user/entity) or spans/anchors?
- How to surface "reasoning_trace" without leaking PII or sensitive traces to end-users? Need scrub rules.
- Integration with rollouts: rulebook versioning + canary (e.g., rulebook:v2 with rollout 5% of traffic).
- Experiment: fast-stream-first strategy where a cheap model produces initial tokens and a stronger model edits/patches. Need latency accounting semantics for billing.

Small experiment plan (1-2 week):
- Build minimal orchestrator shim that accepts inline rulebook + prompt and executes three actions: trim-by-priority, choose-variant, call-model.
- Wire to local dev model variants (gpt-small, gpt-medium) and measure end-to-end p50, p95, token usage for 1000 synthetic prompts.
- Metrics: "goal-satisfaction" rate (e.g., preserved_named_entities), token-savings, extra latency introduced by orchestration.

Random notes to self (brain dump):
- Might reuse parts of existing routing config (tenant-routing-admin-api-proto-slate) but smaller and simpler.
- Add a lightweight "simulator" tool to replay a rulebook against historical traces to estimate token/cost impact before rollout.
- Consider exposing a tiny rules-UI in Console for power users to author/test rulebooks inline.

References / links:
- quick GH PR to start: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestration/pull/458
- related Linear ticket: LINEAR-7890
- sketch Confluence page: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/ORCH-123

If I revisit this: polish the DSL to remove ambiguity around "when" predicates, add example unit tests for each action, and write the simulator harness.
